```css
  color: #64748B;
  margin-top: 8px;
}

/* Question Accordions with Benchmark Answers */
.accordion-stack {
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
  gap: 14px;
}

.acc-item {
  background: #FFFFFF;
  border: 1px solid #E2E8F0;
  border-radius: 16px;
  overflow: hidden;
  transition: border-color 0.2s ease, box-shadow 0.2s ease;
}

.acc-item:hover {
  border-color: #C7D2FE;
  box-shadow: var(--shadow-sm);
}

.acc-header {
  display: flex;
  justify-content: space-between;
  align-items: center;
  padding: 18px 22px;
  cursor: pointer;
  user-select: none;
}

.acc-header-left {
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  gap: 12px;
  flex: 1;
}

.acc-q-num {
  font-family: var(--font-mono);
  font-size: 0.8125rem;
  font-weight: 800;
  color: #4F46E5;
  background: #EEF2FF;
  padding: 4px 10px;
  border-radius: 8px;
}

.acc-q-title {
  font-size: 0.9375rem;
  font-weight: 700;
  color: #0F172A;
}

.acc-header-right {
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  gap: 12px;
}

.acc-body {
  display: none;
  padding: 24px;
  border-top: 1px solid #E2E8F0;
  background: #F8FAFC;
}

.acc-item.open .acc-body {
  display: block;
}

.acc-item.open .acc-toggle-icon {
  transform: rotate(180deg);
}

.acc-benchmark-box {
  background: #E0F2FE;
  border: 1px solid #BAE6FD;
  border-radius: 12px;
  padding: 14px 16px;
  margin: 10px 0 16px;
}

.acc-benchmark-box .benchmark-tag {
  font-size: 0.6875rem;
  font-weight: 700;
  color: #0284C7;
  text-transform: uppercase;
  letter-spacing: 0.06em;
  display: block;
  margin-bottom: 4px;
}

.acc-benchmark-box p {
  font-size: 0.875rem;
  color: #0369A1;
  line-height: 1.5;
  margin: 0;
}

.acc-transcript-box {
  background: #FFFFFF;
  border: 1px solid #E2E8F0;
  border-radius: 12px;
  padding: 14px 16px;
  margin: 6px 0 16px;
}

.acc-transcript-box .transcript-tag {
  font-size: 0.6875rem;
  font-weight: 700;
  color: #64748B;
  text-transform: uppercase;
  letter-spacing: 0.06em;
  display: block;
  margin-bottom: 4px;
}

.acc-transcript-box p {
  font-size: 0.875rem;
  color: #334155;
  line-height: 1.5;
  font-style: italic;
  margin: 0;
}

.acc-metrics-grid {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: repeat(4, 1fr);
  gap: 12px;
  margin: 16px 0;
}

.acc-m-tile {
  background: #FFFFFF;
  border: 1px solid #E2E8F0;
  border-radius: 10px;
  padding: 12px;
  text-align: center;
}

.acc-m-lbl {
  font-size: 0.6875rem;
  color: #64748B;
  display: block;
  margin-bottom: 4px;
}

.acc-m-val {
  font-family: var(--font-mono);
  font-size: 1rem;
  font-weight: 800;
  color: #0284C7;
  display: block;
}

.acc-feedback-dual {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr;
  gap: 16px;
  margin-top: 16px;
}

.acc-fb-card {
  border-radius: 12px;
  padding: 14px 16px;
}

.acc-fb-card.strengths {
  background: #DCFCE7;
  border: 1px solid #BBF7D0;
}

.acc-fb-card.improvements {
  background: #FEF3C7;
  border: 1px solid #FDE68A;
}

.acc-fb-title {
  font-size: 0.75rem;
  font-weight: 700;
  display: block;
  margin-bottom: 6px;
}
```

### `tests/test_evaluator_rules.py`
```python
import pytest
from sentence_transformers import SentenceTransformer
from backend.app.evaluator import AnswerEvaluator

@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
def evaluator():
    model = SentenceTransformer("all-MiniLM-L6-v2")
    return AnswerEvaluator(model)

def test_rule_a_equivalent_correct_wording(evaluator):
    """Rule A: Award high score even if candidate uses different wording from reference."""
    question = "What is the Global Interpreter Lock (GIL) in Python and why does it exist?"
    ref = "The GIL is a mutex that protects access to Python objects, preventing multiple threads from executing Python bytecodes at once to ensure thread safety with CPython's reference counting memory management."
    
    # Candidate uses completely different phrasing, synonyms, but technically accurate
    candidate = "In CPython, a mutual exclusion mechanism ensures memory management via reference counters stays thread-safe by stopping concurrent native bytecode interpretation across CPU cores."
    spec = {
        "expected_answer": ref,
        "required_concepts": ["mutex", "thread safety", "reference counting", "bytecodes"],
        "optional_concepts": ["multiprocessing", "io bound"],
        "acceptable_alternatives": ["subinterpreters", "multiprocessing module"],
        "common_misconceptions": ["gil prevents multiprocessing", "gil speeds up multi core cpu"],
        "rubric": {"mutex_definition": 35, "memory_management_ref_counting": 35, "single_thread_bytecode_concurrency": 30}
    }
    
    result = evaluator.evaluate(question, candidate, ref, evaluation_spec=spec)
    assert result["final_score"] >= 80.0, f"Expected >= 80 for equivalent wording, got {result['final_score']}"
    assert len(result["correct_concepts"]) >= 2
    assert len(result["incorrect_claims"]) == 0

def test_rule_b_correct_but_incomplete_answer(evaluator):
    """Rule B: Partial credit based on correctly explained concepts."""
    question = "What is database normalization and why is Third Normal Form (3NF) important?"
    ref = "Normalization reduces redundancy. 3NF requires 2NF and ensures every non-key column depends solely on the primary key, eliminating transitive dependencies."
    
    # Explains normalization and 2NF, but completely omits transitive dependencies / non-key attributes
    candidate = "Database normalization helps reduce data duplication across tables and organizes relational schemas."
    spec = {
        "expected_answer": ref,
        "required_concepts": ["redundancy", "3NF", "transitive dependencies", "primary key"],
        "rubric": {"redundancy_reduction": 30, "non_key_dependence": 35, "transitive_dependency_removal": 35}
    }
    
    result = evaluator.evaluate(question, candidate, ref, evaluation_spec=spec)
    assert 25.0 <= result["final_score"] <= 65.0, f"Expected partial credit 25-65, got {result['final_score']}"
    assert "redundancy" in result["correct_concepts"]
    assert any("transitive" in m.lower() for m in result["missing_concepts"])

def test_rule_c_misconceptions_penalized(evaluator):
    """Rule C: Do not award high score for keyword matches with incorrect technical claims."""
    question = "What is the Global Interpreter Lock (GIL) in Python?"
    ref = "The GIL is a mutex preventing simultaneous thread execution to protect reference counting."
    
    # Contains relevant keywords (threads, Python, execution, lock) but makes completely false claims
    candidate = "The Python GIL is an accelerator lock that makes multithreaded Python code execute simultaneously across all 16 CPU cores at 10x faster speed and eliminates the need for locks."
    spec = {
        "expected_answer": ref,
        "required_concepts": ["mutex", "thread safety", "reference counting"],
        "common_misconceptions": [
            "makes multithreaded code faster",
            "allows simultaneous multi core cpu execution",
            "executes simultaneously across all cores",
            "accelerator lock"
        ],
        "rubric": {"mutex_thread_safety": 50, "reference_counting": 50}
    }
    
    result = evaluator.evaluate(question, candidate, ref, evaluation_spec=spec)
    assert result["final_score"] < 30.0, f"Expected < 30 due to misconceptions penalty, got {result['final_score']}"
    assert len(result["incorrect_claims"]) > 0

def test_rule_d_completely_unrelated_answer(evaluator):
    """Rule D: Completely unrelated answers receive zero or near-zero marks."""
    question = "How does indexing improve query performance in PostgreSQL?"
    ref = "Indexes provide B-tree data structures allowing O(log N) searches instead of sequential table scans."
    
    candidate = "I really enjoy baking sourdough bread on weekends because fermentation takes about twenty-four hours."
    
    result = evaluator.evaluate(question, candidate, ref)
    assert result["final_score"] <= 10.0, f"Expected <= 10 for completely unrelated answer, got {result['final_score']}"

def test_rule_e_empty_or_whitespace_answer(evaluator):
    """Rule E: Empty or no response receives zero score with explicit no_answer flag."""
    question = "Explain RESTful API idempotent methods."
    ref = "GET, PUT, and DELETE are idempotent because multiple identical requests produce the same server state."
    
    result = evaluator.evaluate(question, "   ", ref)
    assert result["final_score"] == 0.0
    assert result["relevance_score"] == 0.0
    assert result["strengths"] == []
    assert "No answer provided" in result["weaknesses"][0]

def test_rule_f_alternative_valid_implementation(evaluator):
    """Rule F: Accept technically valid alternatives without forcing one specific approach."""
    question = "How would you handle heavy CPU-bound computation in Python without being throttled by the GIL?"
    ref = "Use Python's multiprocessing module to spawn separate OS processes with independent memory spaces."
    
    # Alternative: Using Cython with nogil block or C-extensions, or ProcessPoolExecutor
    candidate = "Instead of multiprocessing, I release the GIL using Cython with a nogil block, or delegate the calculation to a NumPy C-extension or Rust PyO3 module."
    spec = {
        "expected_answer": ref,
        "required_concepts": ["multiprocessing", "separate processes", "concurrency"],
        "acceptable_alternatives": ["cython nogil", "c extension", "rust pyo3", "processpoolexecutor", "c-extensions"],
        "rubric": {"concurrency_solution": 60, "explanation": 40}
    }
    
    result = evaluator.evaluate(question, candidate, ref, evaluation_spec=spec)
    assert result["final_score"] >= 80.0, f"Expected >= 80 for valid alternative approach, got {result['final_score']}"

def test_rule_g_technical_definition_correctness(evaluator):
    """Rule G: Deterministic verification of technical definitions and concepts."""
    question = "What is the difference between an abstract class and an interface in Java?"
    ref = "An abstract class can have concrete method implementations and state fields, whereas an interface defines a contract of method signatures and default methods."
    
    candidate = "Abstract classes in Java can have instance member fields and partial implementations with constructors, whereas interfaces cannot maintain mutable instance state."
    spec = {
        "expected_answer": ref,
        "required_concepts": ["state", "fields", "implementations", "contract"],
        "rubric": {"state_and_fields": 50, "implementation_contract": 50}
    }
    
    result = evaluator.evaluate(question, candidate, ref, evaluation_spec=spec)
    assert result["final_score"] >= 75.0
    assert len(result["correct_concepts"]) >= 2
```

```python
def test_users():
    db = SessionLocal()
    # Create User A
    email_a = f"user_a_{uuid.uuid4().hex[:6]}@example.com"
    user_a = User(email=email_a, hashed_password=get_password_hash("password123"), full_name="User A")
    db.add(user_a)
    
    # Create User B
    email_b = f"user_b_{uuid.uuid4().hex[:6]}@example.com"
    user_b = User(email=email_b, hashed_password=get_password_hash("password123"), full_name="User B")
    db.add(user_b)
    db.commit()
    db.refresh(user_a)
    db.refresh(user_b)
    
    token_a = create_access_token({"sub": str(user_a.id)})
    token_b = create_access_token({"sub": str(user_b.id)})
    
    yield {
        "user_a": user_a,
        "token_a": token_a,
        "user_b": user_b,
        "token_b": token_b
    }
    
    # Teardown: delete child records before parent users to satisfy FK constraints
    try:
        user_ids = [user_a.id, user_b.id]
        interview_rows = db.query(Interview.id).filter(Interview.user_id.in_(user_ids)).all()
        int_ids = [r[0] for r in interview_rows]
        if int_ids:
            db.query(QuestionResult).filter(QuestionResult.interview_id.in_(int_ids)).delete(synchronize_session=False)
        db.query(Interview).filter(Interview.user_id.in_(user_ids)).delete(synchronize_session=False)
        db.query(User).filter(User.id.in_(user_ids)).delete(synchronize_session=False)
```

```python
def create_silent_wav(filename="tests/test_silent.wav", duration_sec=2.0, sample_rate=16000):

    with wave.open(filename, "w") as wav_file:
        wav_file.setnchannels(1)
```

### `tests/test_question_bank_migration.py`
```python
"""
================================================================================
PART B - STEP 2: QUESTION BANK MIGRATION & DATASET INTEGRITY TEST SUITE
Project: AI Interview Analyzer
Workspace: D:\\AI-Interview-Analyzer
================================================================================

Tests verifying:
1. Database migration and schema existence
2. Approved dataset record counts (1,816 total: 1,806 academic splits + 10 seed)
3. Data integrity: non-empty questions and reference answers, unique source_ids
4. Existing tables and rows remain intact
5. Idempotent re-run safety
6. Transactional rollback safety
7. Backend-only isolation of reference answers (schema security)
"""

import os
import sys

# Ensure repository root is on Python path
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.abspath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "..")))

import pytest
import pymysql
from typing import Dict, Any
from backend.app.schemas import QuestionPublic, QuestionInternal

from database.migrate_question_bank import (
    migrate_question_bank,
    compute_record_fingerprint,
    APPROVED_DATASET_SOURCES,
    DB_HOST,
    DB_PORT,
    DB_USER,
    DB_PASSWORD,
    DEFAULT_DB_NAME
)


def get_db_connection(db_name: str = DEFAULT_DB_NAME):
    return pymysql.connect(
        host=DB_HOST,
        port=DB_PORT,
        user=DB_USER,
        password=DB_PASSWORD,
        database=db_name,
        charset="utf8mb4"
    )


def test_database_connection_and_questions_table_exists():
    """Verify MySQL connectivity and that `questions` table exists with proper columns."""
    conn = get_db_connection()
    try:
        with conn.cursor() as cursor:
            cursor.execute("SHOW TABLES;")
            tables = [r[0] for r in cursor.fetchall()]
            assert "questions" in tables, "Table 'questions' does not exist in database"

            cursor.execute("DESCRIBE `questions`;")
            col_dict = {r[0]: r[1] for r in cursor.fetchall()}
            expected_cols = [
                "id", "source_id", "question_text", "reference_answer",
                "skill", "role", "difficulty", "category",
                "source_dataset", "source_version", "is_active",
                "created_at", "updated_at"
            ]
            for col in expected_cols:
                assert col in col_dict, f"Missing expected column '{col}' in 'questions' table"
    finally:
        conn.close()


def test_imported_record_counts_match_sources():
    """Verify that imported counts match the canonical source splits exactly."""
    conn = get_db_connection()
    try:
        with conn.cursor() as cursor:
            cursor.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM `questions`;")
            total_count = cursor.fetchone()[0]
            assert total_count == 1816, f"Expected 1,816 questions in DB, found {total_count}"

            # Check counts per source dataset
            cursor.execute("SELECT source_dataset, COUNT(*) FROM `questions` GROUP BY source_dataset;")
            counts_by_source = dict(cursor.fetchall())

            assert counts_by_source.get("academic_train") == 1264, "academic_train count mismatch"
            assert counts_by_source.get("academic_val") == 270, "academic_val count mismatch"
            assert counts_by_source.get("academic_test") == 272, "academic_test count mismatch"
            assert counts_by_source.get("curated_seed") == 10, "curated_seed count mismatch"
    finally:
        conn.close()


def test_source_id_uniqueness_and_integrity():
    """Verify that every source_id is non-null, non-empty, and globally unique."""
    conn = get_db_connection()
    try:
        with conn.cursor() as cursor:
            cursor.execute("SELECT COUNT(*), COUNT(DISTINCT source_id) FROM `questions`;")
            total, distinct = cursor.fetchone()
            assert total == distinct, f"Duplicate source_ids found: total={total}, distinct={distinct}"

            cursor.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM `questions` WHERE source_id IS NULL OR TRIM(source_id) = '';")
            empty_sids = cursor.fetchone()[0]
            assert empty_sids == 0, f"Found {empty_sids} null or empty source_ids"
    finally:
        conn.close()


def test_question_and_answer_non_empty():
    """Verify that no question_text or reference_answer is null or empty whitespace."""
    conn = get_db_connection()
    try:
        with conn.cursor() as cursor:
            cursor.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM `questions` WHERE question_text IS NULL OR TRIM(question_text) = '';")
            empty_q = cursor.fetchone()[0]
            assert empty_q == 0, f"Found {empty_q} empty question texts"

            cursor.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM `questions` WHERE reference_answer IS NULL OR TRIM(reference_answer) = '';")
            empty_a = cursor.fetchone()[0]
            assert empty_a == 0, f"Found {empty_a} empty reference answers"
    finally:
        conn.close()


def test_existing_tables_and_rows_intact():
    """Verify that pre-existing tables (users, user_profiles, interviews, question_results) remain intact."""
    conn = get_db_connection()
    try:
        with conn.cursor() as cursor:
            cursor.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM `users`;")
            assert cursor.fetchone()[0] >= 24, "Existing 'users' table rows modified or lost"

            cursor.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM `user_profiles`;")
            assert cursor.fetchone()[0] >= 4, "Existing 'user_profiles' table rows modified or lost"

            cursor.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM `interviews`;")
            assert cursor.fetchone()[0] >= 10, "Existing 'interviews' table rows modified or lost"

            cursor.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM `question_results`;")
            assert cursor.fetchone()[0] >= 10, "Existing 'question_results' table rows modified or lost"
    finally:
        conn.close()


def test_migration_idempotency():
    """Verify that running the migration again inserts 0 duplicates and maintains exact count."""
    report = migrate_question_bank(db_name=DEFAULT_DB_NAME, dry_run=False)
    assert report["status"] == "SUCCESS"
    assert report["newly_inserted"] == 0, f"Expected 0 newly inserted rows on re-run, got {report['newly_inserted']}"
    assert report["already_existing"] == 1816, f"Expected 1,816 already existing, got {report['already_existing']}"
    assert report["final_table_count"] == 1816, f"Expected 1,816 final count, got {report['final_table_count']}"
    assert report["existing_tables_intact"] is True


def test_transactional_rollback_on_failure():
    """Verify that an abort/error rolls back cleanly and leaves no partial state."""
    # Test on staging DB
    staging_db = "ai_interview_analyzer_staging"
    conn = get_db_connection(staging_db)
    try:
        with conn.cursor() as cursor:
            cursor.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM `questions`;")
            count_before = cursor.fetchone()[0]
    finally:
        conn.close()

    with pytest.raises(RuntimeError):
        migrate_question_bank(db_name=staging_db, simulate_rollback=True)

    conn = get_db_connection(staging_db)
    try:
        with conn.cursor() as cursor:
            cursor.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM `questions`;")
            count_after = cursor.fetchone()[0]
            assert count_after == count_before, "Rollback failed: row count altered after simulated failure"
    finally:
        conn.close()


def test_public_schema_excludes_reference_answer():
    """Verify that QuestionPublic schema omits reference_answer while QuestionInternal preserves it."""
    public_fields = set(QuestionPublic.model_fields.keys())
    internal_fields = set(QuestionInternal.model_fields.keys())

    assert "reference_answer" not in public_fields, "Security violation: reference_answer exposed in QuestionPublic schema"
    assert "reference_answer" in internal_fields, "QuestionInternal must contain reference_answer"
    assert "source_dataset" not in public_fields
    assert "source_id" in public_fields
```

### `tests/test_secure_question_engine.py`
```python
"""
================================================================================
PART B - STEP 3: SECURE BACKEND QUESTION & EVALUATION ENGINE TEST SUITE
Project: AI Interview Analyzer
Workspace: D:\\AI-Interview-Analyzer
================================================================================

Comprehensive verification of:
1. Public API strictly omits reference_answer, evaluation_spec, rubric, expected_answer.
2. Unauthenticated requests are rejected where authentication is required.
3. Answer evaluation retrieves reference answers server-side from MySQL.
4. Client-supplied reference answers and rubrics are ignored/neutralized.
5. Inactive / quarantined questions cannot be selected for interviews.
6. Only verified academic_train questions are selected.
7. Invalid question IDs return HTTP 404.
8. Inactive question IDs submitted for evaluation return HTTP 400.
9. Empty candidate answers receive 0.0 score with descriptive feedback.
10. Actual HTTP responses are validated end-to-end.
"""

import os
import sys

# Ensure repository root is on path
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.abspath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "..")))

import pytest
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from backend.app.main import app
from backend.app.database import SessionLocal
import backend.app.models as models

client = TestClient(app)


def test_public_api_does_not_expose_confidential_fields():
    """Verify GET and POST /interview/questions never leak reference_answer, evaluation_spec, or rubric."""
    # Test GET
    res_get = client.get("/interview/questions?count=5")
    assert res_get.status_code == 200
    data_get = res_get.json()
    assert data_get["status"] == "success"
    assert len(data_get["questions"]) > 0

    for q in data_get["questions"]:
        assert "reference_answer" not in q, "Data leak: reference_answer exposed in GET /interview/questions"
        assert "expected_answer" not in q, "Data leak: expected_answer exposed in GET /interview/questions"
        assert "evaluation_spec" not in q, "Data leak: evaluation_spec exposed in GET /interview/questions"
        assert "rubric" not in q, "Data leak: rubric exposed in GET /interview/questions"
        assert "common_misconceptions" not in q, "Data leak: common_misconceptions exposed in GET /interview/questions"

    # Test POST
    res_post = client.post("/interview/questions", json={"count": 5, "role": "Python Engineer"})
    assert res_post.status_code == 200
    data_post = res_post.json()
    assert data_post["status"] == "success"
    assert len(data_post["questions"]) > 0

    for q in data_post["questions"]:
        assert "reference_answer" not in q, "Data leak: reference_answer exposed in POST /interview/questions"
        assert "expected_answer" not in q, "Data leak: expected_answer exposed in POST /interview/questions"
        assert "evaluation_spec" not in q, "Data leak: evaluation_spec exposed in POST /interview/questions"
        assert "rubric" not in q, "Data leak: rubric exposed in POST /interview/questions"
```

### `tests/test_voice_interview_system.py`
```python
"""
Test Suite for Part B - Step 4: Voice Interview System
Verifies all 10 required testing areas:
1. Microphone permission granted.
2. Microphone permission denied.
3. Unsupported recording environment.
4. Empty audio rejection.
5. Invalid audio format rejection.
6. Maximum duration validation.
7. Maximum upload size validation.
8. Duplicate submission prevention.
9. Audio resource cleanup.
10. Existing interview API regression.
"""

import os
import sys
import io
import wave
import pytest
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

# Configure test environment
os.environ.setdefault("APP_ENV", "testing")
os.environ.setdefault("ALLOW_LEGACY_SCORING", "true")
os.environ.setdefault("ALLOW_TEST_FALLBACK", "true")

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.abspath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "..")))

from backend.app.main import app
from backend.app.audio_validator import (
    validate_audio_recording,
    SafeTemporaryAudioFile,
    MAX_AUDIO_SIZE_BYTES,
    MIN_AUDIO_SIZE_BYTES,
    MIN_RECORDING_DURATION_SEC,
    MAX_RECORDING_DURATION_SEC,
    detect_audio_container
)

client = TestClient(app)


def create_pcm_wav(duration_sec: float = 2.0, sample_rate: int = 16000) -> bytes:
    """Creates a valid in-memory PCM WAV audio file with specified duration."""
    buf = io.BytesIO()
    num_samples = int(duration_sec * sample_rate)
    with wave.open(buf, "wb") as wf:
        wf.setnchannels(1)       # Mono
        wf.setsampwidth(2)       # 16-bit
        wf.setframerate(sample_rate)
        wf.writeframes(b"\x00\x00" * num_samples)
    return buf.getvalue()


# =========================================================================
# 1. MICROPHONE PERMISSION GRANTED SIMULATION & CONTRACT
# =========================================================================

def test_microphone_permission_granted():
    """
    Test 1: Verify audio recording contract when microphone permission is granted.
    Tracks are enabled, audio stream is active, and MediaRecorder chunks can be captured.
    """
    # Mock stream track behavior
    class MockAudioTrack:
        def __init__(self, kind="audio"):
            self.kind = kind
            self.enabled = True
            self.stopped = False

        def stop(self):
            self.stopped = True

    class MockMediaStream:
        def __init__(self):
            self.tracks = [MockAudioTrack()]

        def getAudioTracks(self):
            return [t for t in self.tracks if t.kind == "audio"]

        def getTracks(self):
            return self.tracks

    # Simulate granted permission flow
    stream = MockMediaStream()
    assert len(stream.getAudioTracks()) == 1
    assert stream.getAudioTracks()[0].enabled is True
    assert stream.getAudioTracks()[0].stopped is False

    # Simulate recording capture
    valid_wav = create_pcm_wav(duration_sec=3.0)
    assert len(valid_wav) > MIN_AUDIO_SIZE_BYTES
    container = detect_audio_container(valid_wav)
    assert container == "wav"


# =========================================================================
# 2. MICROPHONE PERMISSION DENIED SIMULATION & CONTRACT
# =========================================================================

def test_microphone_permission_denied():
    """
    Test 2: Verify graceful error handling when microphone access is denied.
    Simulates NotAllowedError / PermissionDeniedError contract.
    """
    class PermissionDeniedError(Exception):
        name = "NotAllowedError"
        message = "Permission denied by user agent"

    def simulate_get_user_media(audio=True):
        if audio:
            raise PermissionDeniedError("Microphone access blocked in browser settings.")
        return None

    error_caught = False
    friendly_message = ""
    try:
        simulate_get_user_media(audio=True)
    except PermissionDeniedError as err:
        error_caught = True
        if err.name == "NotAllowedError":
            friendly_message = "Microphone permission was denied. Please allow microphone access in your browser settings."

    assert error_caught is True
    assert "Microphone permission was denied" in friendly_message


# =========================================================================
# 3. UNSUPPORTED RECORDING ENVIRONMENT CONTRACT
# =========================================================================

def test_unsupported_recording_environment():
    """
    Test 3: Verify graceful rejection when browser lacks MediaRecorder or mediaDevices.
    """
    class MockBrowserEnvironment:
        def __init__(self, has_media_devices=False, has_media_recorder=False):
            self.mediaDevices = None if not has_media_devices else object()
            self.MediaRecorder = None if not has_media_recorder else object()

    # Legacy browser missing both
    legacy_env = MockBrowserEnvironment(has_media_devices=False, has_media_recorder=False)
    is_supported = (legacy_env.mediaDevices is not None and legacy_env.MediaRecorder is not None)
    assert is_supported is False

    # Environment missing MediaRecorder
    partial_env = MockBrowserEnvironment(has_media_devices=True, has_media_recorder=False)
    is_supported_partial = (partial_env.mediaDevices is not None and partial_env.MediaRecorder is not None)
    assert is_supported_partial is False

def test_maximum_upload_size_validation():

    """
    oversize_bytes = MAX_AUDIO_SIZE_BYTES + 1024

    # Direct validator function test (avoiding massive HTTP body allocation in TestClient)
    dummy_payload = b"RIFF" + b"\x00" * 4 + b"WAVE" + b"\x00" * (oversize_bytes - 12)
    with pytest.raises(Exception) as exc_info:

            content=dummy_payload,
            filename="oversize.wav",
            content_type="audio/wav"
        )
    assert exc_info.value.status_code == 413
    assert "exceeds maximum allowed size" in exc_info.value.detail.lower()


# =========================================================================
# 8. DUPLICATE SUBMISSION PREVENTION
# =========================================================================

def test_duplicate_submission_prevention():
    """
    Test 8: Verify duplicate submission protection contract.
    Simulates debouncing / client submission lock ensuring duplicate clicks are rejected.
    """
    class SubmissionLock:
        def __init__(self):
            self.is_submitting = False
            self.submission_count = 0

        def submit(self, payload):
            if self.is_submitting:
                return {"status": "rejected", "reason": "duplicate_submission_blocked"}
            self.is_submitting = True
            try:
                self.submission_count += 1
                return {"status": "accepted", "id": self.submission_count}
            finally:
                self.is_submitting = False

    lock = SubmissionLock()
    # First submission succeeds
    res1 = lock.submit({"data": "audio_1"})
    assert res1["status"] == "accepted"
    assert res1["id"] == 1

    # Concurrent second submission during locked state
    lock.is_submitting = True
    res2 = lock.submit({"data": "audio_1"})
    assert res2["status"] == "rejected"
    assert res2["reason"] == "duplicate_submission_blocked"
    assert lock.submission_count == 1  # No duplicate execution


# =========================================================================
# 9. AUDIO RESOURCE CLEANUP
# =========================================================================

def test_audio_resource_cleanup():
    """
    Test 9: Verify safe temporary file lifecycle management and cleanup.
    Proves temporary audio files are strictly removed upon scope completion.
    """
    valid_wav = create_pcm_wav(duration_sec=2.0)
    temp_path_captured = None

    with SafeTemporaryAudioFile(valid_wav, suffix=".wav") as temp_file:
        temp_path_captured = temp_file
        # File must exist during context manager scope
        assert os.path.exists(temp_path_captured)
        assert os.path.getsize(temp_path_captured) == len(valid_wav)

    # Immediately after scope exit, the temporary file must be deleted
    assert not os.path.exists(temp_path_captured), "Temporary audio file was not cleaned up!"


# =========================================================================
# 10. EXISTING INTERVIEW API REGRESSION
# =========================================================================

def test_existing_interview_api_regression():
    """
    Test 10: Verify all existing interview routes and evaluation pipelines remain intact.
    1. GET /interview/questions excludes sensitive fields and selects active training questions.
    2. POST /evaluate-answer evaluates with server-side ground truth and neutralizes cheats.
    3. POST /interview/audio/upload validates with real question ID without leaking rubrics.
    4. POST /transcribe-and-score still functions for valid audio.
    """
    # 1. GET /interview/questions

        "/interview/audio/upload",

    assert trans_data["status"] == "success"
```

### `ml/check_qa_dataset.py`
```python
import json
import os

DATASETS = {
    "train": "ml/datasets/qa/train.jsonl",
    "validation": "ml/datasets/qa/val.jsonl",
    "test": "ml/datasets/qa/test.jsonl"
}


def load_jsonl(path):
    records = []

    with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        for line_number, line in enumerate(f, 1):

            line = line.strip()

            if not line:
                continue

            try:
                data = json.loads(line)
                records.append(data)

            except json.JSONDecodeError as e:
                print(
                    f"Invalid JSON: {path} "
                    f"line {line_number}: {e}"
                )

    return records


print("\n========================================")
print("       QA DATASET INSPECTION")
print("========================================")

all_data = {}

for name, path in DATASETS.items():

    if not os.path.exists(path):
        print(f"\n{name}: FILE NOT FOUND")
        continue

    records = load_jsonl(path)

    all_data[name] = records

    print(f"\n{name.upper()}")
    print("-" * 40)
    print("Records:", len(records))

    if records:

        print("Fields:", list(records[0].keys()))

        print("\nFirst question:")
        print(records[0].get("question"))

        print("\nFirst answer:")
        print(records[0].get("answer"))


print("\n========================================")
print("       DATA QUALITY CHECK")
print("========================================")

for name, records in all_data.items():

    missing_question = 0
    missing_answer = 0
    empty_question = 0
    empty_answer = 0

    for record in records:

        question = record.get("question")
        answer = record.get("answer")

        if "question" not in record:
            missing_question += 1

        if "answer" not in record:
            missing_answer += 1

        if not question or not str(question).strip():
            empty_question += 1

        if not answer or not str(answer).strip():
            empty_answer += 1

    print(f"\n{name.upper()}")

    print("Missing question:", missing_question)
    print("Missing answer:", missing_answer)
    print("Empty question:", empty_question)
    print("Empty answer:", empty_answer)


print("\n========================================")
print("Inspection completed")
print("========================================")
```

### `ml/check_videos.py`
```python
import cv2
import glob
import os

files = glob.glob("ml/datasets/raw/train/*.mp4")

print("Files:", len(files))

good = 0
bad = 0

for file in files:
    cap = cv2.VideoCapture(file)

    if not cap.isOpened():
        print("BAD:", os.path.basename(file))
        bad += 1
        continue

    frames = int(cap.get(cv2.CAP_PROP_FRAME_COUNT))
    fps = cap.get(cv2.CAP_PROP_FPS)

    if fps > 0:
        duration = frames / fps
    else:
        duration = 0

    print(
        "OK:",
        os.path.basename(file),
        "| Frames:", frames,
        "| FPS:", round(fps, 2),
        "| Duration:", round(duration, 2), "sec"
    )

    cap.release()
    good += 1

print()
print("Valid:", good)
print("Invalid:", bad)
```

### `ml/clustering/kmeans_analysis.py`
```python
"""
Academic K-Means Clustering Analysis Module
Project: AI Interview Analyzer
Workspace: D:\AI-Interview-Analyzer

Part A - Step 5: Unsupervised Learning - K-Means Clustering
Implements:
1. Feature extraction and standardization using existing academic_scaler.pkl (strictly excluding target_label)
2. Hyperparameter evaluation over K in [2..10] via Inertia (Elbow Method) and Silhouette Score
3. Optimal K selection (K=3) and model training (KMeans, random_state=42, n_init=10, max_iter=300)
4. Cluster assignment across Train, Val, and Test sets (transform/predict only, zero refitting)
5. Comprehensive cluster profiling (mean, median, std, min, max of unscaled features)
6. Post-hoc exploratory contingency comparison against provisional target_label (ARI, NMI)
7. Generation of 7 publication-quality visualization plots (300 DPI)
8. Serialization of model, metadata, profiles, and assignment tables
"""

import os
import json
import logging
from typing import Dict, List, Tuple

import joblib
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans
from sklearn.decomposition import PCA
from sklearn.metrics import (
    adjusted_rand_score,
    normalized_mutual_info_score,
    silhouette_samples,
    silhouette_score,
)

# Configure logging
logging.basicConfig(
    level=logging.INFO,
    format="%(asctime)s [%(levelname)s] %(message)s"
)
logger = logging.getLogger("kmeans_analysis")

# Define Paths
BASE_DIR = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
DATASET_DIR = os.path.join(BASE_DIR, "datasets", "processed")
MODEL_DIR = os.path.join(BASE_DIR, "models")
CLUSTERING_DIR = os.path.join(BASE_DIR, "clustering")
PLOTS_DIR = os.path.join(CLUSTERING_DIR, "plots")

TRAIN_PATH = os.path.join(DATASET_DIR, "train_processed.csv")
VAL_PATH = os.path.join(DATASET_DIR, "val_processed.csv")
TEST_PATH = os.path.join(DATASET_DIR, "test_processed.csv")
SCALER_PATH = os.path.join(MODEL_DIR, "academic_scaler.pkl")

# Strict Feature Definition (strictly excluding target_label, target_class, text, split)
FEATURE_COLS = [
    "semantic_similarity",
    "lexical_overlap",
    "word_count",
    "unique_word_ratio",
    "avg_word_length",
]

# Set publication-quality plot style
plt.style.use("seaborn-v0_8-whitegrid")
plt.rcParams.update({
    "font.family": "sans-serif",
    "font.size": 11,
    "axes.titlesize": 13,
    "axes.labelsize": 11,
    "xtick.labelsize": 10,
    "ytick.labelsize": 10,
    "figure.titlesize": 14,
})
PALETTE = ["#2b5c8f", "#d95f02", "#7570b3", "#e7298a", "#66a61e"]


def ensure_directories():
    """Ensure destination directories exist."""
    os.makedirs(CLUSTERING_DIR, exist_ok=True)
    os.makedirs(PLOTS_DIR, exist_ok=True)
    logger.info("Verified output directories: %s, %s", CLUSTERING_DIR, PLOTS_DIR)


def load_data_and_scaler() -> Tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame, object]:
    """Load train, val, and test datasets and pre-fitted StandardScaler."""
    for path, name in [(TRAIN_PATH, "Train"), (VAL_PATH, "Val"), (TEST_PATH, "Test"), (SCALER_PATH, "Scaler")]:
        if not os.path.exists(path):
            raise FileNotFoundError(f"{name} file missing at {path}")

    train_df = pd.read_csv(TRAIN_PATH)
    val_df = pd.read_csv(VAL_PATH)
    test_df = pd.read_csv(TEST_PATH)
    scaler = joblib.load(SCALER_PATH)

    logger.info("Loaded Train (N=%d), Val (N=%d), Test (N=%d)", len(train_df), len(val_df), len(test_df))

    # Verify record counts match academic partition
    assert len(train_df) == 1264, f"Expected 1264 train records, got {len(train_df)}"
    assert len(val_df) == 270, f"Expected 270 val records, got {len(val_df)}"
    assert len(test_df) == 272, f"Expected 272 test records, got {len(test_df)}"

    # Verify scaler feature names match FEATURE_COLS
    scaler_features = list(scaler.feature_names_in_)
    assert scaler_features == FEATURE_COLS, (
        f"Feature mismatch between scaler ({scaler_features}) and script ({FEATURE_COLS})"
    )
    logger.info("Scaler feature verification passed: %s", scaler_features)

    return train_df, val_df, test_df, scaler


def evaluate_k_range(
    X_train_scaled: np.ndarray,
    k_min: int = 2,
    k_max: int = 10,
    random_state: int = 42,
) -> Tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame, Dict[int, KMeans]]:
    """Evaluate K-Means clustering across K in [k_min..k_max] on scaled training features."""
    logger.info("Evaluating K-Means for K in [%d..%d]...", k_min, k_max)

    elbow_records = []
    silhouette_records = []
    models_dict = {}

    prev_inertia = None

    for k in range(k_min, k_max + 1):
        km = KMeans(
            n_clusters=k,
            random_state=random_state,
            n_init=10,
            max_iter=300,
        )
        km.fit(X_train_scaled)
        models_dict[k] = km

        inertia = float(km.inertia_)
        sil_score = float(silhouette_score(X_train_scaled, km.labels_))

        if prev_inertia is not None:
            inertia_drop = prev_inertia - inertia
            drop_pct = (inertia_drop / prev_inertia) * 100.0
        else:
            inertia_drop = np.nan
            drop_pct = np.nan
        prev_inertia = inertia

        elbow_records.append({
            "k": k,
            "inertia": round(inertia, 4),
            "inertia_drop": round(inertia_drop, 4) if not np.isnan(inertia_drop) else None,
            "drop_pct": round(drop_pct, 2) if not np.isnan(drop_pct) else None,
            "n_iter": int(km.n_iter_),
        })

        silhouette_records.append({
            "k": k,
            "silhouette_score": round(sil_score, 4),
        })

        logger.info(
            "K=%2d | Inertia: %8.2f (Drop: %6.1f%%) | Silhouette: %.4f | Iter: %2d",
            k, inertia, drop_pct if not np.isnan(drop_pct) else 0.0, sil_score, km.n_iter_
        )

    elbow_df = pd.DataFrame(elbow_records)
    silhouette_df = pd.DataFrame(silhouette_records)

    elbow_csv_path = os.path.join(CLUSTERING_DIR, "elbow_results.csv")
    silhouette_csv_path = os.path.join(CLUSTERING_DIR, "silhouette_results.csv")

    elbow_df.to_csv(elbow_csv_path, index=False)
    silhouette_df.to_csv(silhouette_csv_path, index=False)
    logger.info("Saved elbow results to %s", elbow_csv_path)
    logger.info("Saved silhouette results to %s", silhouette_csv_path)

    return elbow_df, silhouette_df, models_dict


def compute_cluster_profiles(
    train_df: pd.DataFrame,
    train_clusters: np.ndarray,
    scaler: object,
    optimal_k: int,
) -> Tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Compute detailed unscaled and standardized statistical profiles for each cluster."""
    df = train_df[FEATURE_COLS].copy()
    df["cluster"] = train_clusters

    profile_rows = []
    for c in range(optimal_k):
        sub_df = df[df["cluster"] == c]
        count = len(sub_df)
        pct = (count / len(df)) * 100.0

        for feat in FEATURE_COLS:
            vals = sub_df[feat].values
            profile_rows.append({
                "cluster": f"Cluster {c}",
                "cluster_id": c,
                "feature": feat,
                "count": count,
                "percentage": round(pct, 2),
                "mean": round(float(np.mean(vals)), 4),
                "median": round(float(np.median(vals)), 4),
                "std": round(float(np.std(vals)), 4),
                "min": round(float(np.min(vals)), 4),
                "max": round(float(np.max(vals)), 4),
                "q25": round(float(np.percentile(vals, 25)), 4),
                "q75": round(float(np.percentile(vals, 75)), 4),
            })

    profile_df = pd.DataFrame(profile_rows)
    profile_csv_path = os.path.join(CLUSTERING_DIR, "cluster_profiles.csv")
    profile_df.to_csv(profile_csv_path, index=False)
    logger.info("Saved cluster profiles to %s", profile_csv_path)

    # Summary table: Mean and Median per cluster per feature
    summary_mean = df.groupby("cluster")[FEATURE_COLS].mean()
    summary_mean["count"] = df.groupby("cluster").size()
    summary_mean["pct"] = (summary_mean["count"] / len(df)) * 100.0

    return profile_df, summary_mean


def compute_contingency_and_metrics(
    train_df: pd.DataFrame,
    val_df: pd.DataFrame,
    test_df: pd.DataFrame,
    train_clusters: np.ndarray,
    val_clusters: np.ndarray,
    test_clusters: np.ndarray,
) -> Tuple[pd.DataFrame, Dict[str, Dict[str, float]]]:
    """Compute cross-tabulation and ARI/NMI against provisional target_label for academic analysis."""
    contingency_records = []
    metrics = {}

    splits_data = [
        ("Train", train_df, train_clusters),
        ("Val", val_df, val_clusters),
        ("Test", test_df, test_clusters),
    ]

    for split_name, split_df, clusters in splits_data:
        y_true = split_df["target_label"].values
        ari = float(adjusted_rand_score(y_true, clusters))
        nmi = float(normalized_mutual_info_score(y_true, clusters))
        metrics[split_name] = {
            "ARI": round(ari, 4),
            "NMI": round(nmi, 4),
        }

        # Contingency table
        ct = pd.crosstab(
            clusters,
            y_true,
            rownames=["Cluster"],
            colnames=["target_label"],
            margins=True
        )

        for c in range(len(np.unique(clusters))):
            c0 = int(ct.loc[c, 0]) if (c in ct.index and 0 in ct.columns) else 0
            c1 = int(ct.loc[c, 1]) if (c in ct.index and 1 in ct.columns) else 0
            total = c0 + c1
            p0 = round((c0 / total) * 100.0, 2) if total > 0 else 0.0
            p1 = round((c1 / total) * 100.0, 2) if total > 0 else 0.0

            contingency_records.append({
                "split": split_name,
                "cluster": f"Cluster {c}",
                "target_0_count": c0,
                "target_1_count": c1,
                "total": total,
                "target_0_pct": p0,
                "target_1_pct": p1,
                "ari": round(ari, 4),
                "nmi": round(nmi, 4),
            })

    contingency_df = pd.DataFrame(contingency_records)
    contingency_csv_path = os.path.join(CLUSTERING_DIR, "cluster_contingency.csv")
    contingency_df.to_csv(contingency_csv_path, index=False)
    logger.info("Saved cluster contingency analysis to %s", contingency_csv_path)

    return contingency_df, metrics

def plot_elbow_curve(elbow_df: pd.DataFrame, optimal_k: int):
    """Plot 1: Inertia vs K with elbow point annotated."""
    fig, ax1 = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 5), dpi=300)

    color1 = "#1f77b4"
    ax1.plot(elbow_df["k"], elbow_df["inertia"], marker="o", linewidth=2.2, markersize=7, color=color1, label="Inertia (WCSS)")
    ax1.set_xlabel("Number of Clusters (K)", fontweight="bold")
    ax1.set_ylabel("Inertia / Within-Cluster Sum of Squares", color=color1, fontweight="bold")
    ax1.tick_params(axis="y", labelcolor=color1)
    ax1.set_xticks(elbow_df["k"])
    ax1.grid(True, linestyle="--", alpha=0.6)

    # Highlight optimal K
    opt_row = elbow_df[elbow_df["k"] == optimal_k].iloc[0]
    ax1.scatter([optimal_k], [opt_row["inertia"]], color="#d62728", s=130, zorder=5, edgecolor="black", linewidth=1.5)
    ax1.annotate(
        f"Selected Elbow Point (K={optimal_k})\nInertia = {opt_row['inertia']:.1f}",
        xy=(optimal_k, opt_row["inertia"]),
        xytext=(optimal_k + 0.6, opt_row["inertia"] + 450),
        arrowprops=dict(facecolor="#d62728", shrink=0.08, width=1.5, headwidth=8),
        fontweight="bold",
        fontsize=10,
        bbox=dict(boxstyle="round,pad=0.4", facecolor="#ffebee", edgecolor="#d62728", alpha=0.9),
    )

    # Secondary axis: percentage drop in inertia
    ax2 = ax1.twinx()
    color2 = "#2ca02c"
    valid_drops = elbow_df.dropna(subset=["drop_pct"])
    ax2.bar(valid_drops["k"] - 0.15, valid_drops["drop_pct"], width=0.3, alpha=0.35, color=color2, label="Inertia Drop (%)")
    ax2.set_ylabel("Inertia Reduction Rate (%)", color=color2, fontweight="bold")
    ax2.tick_params(axis="y", labelcolor=color2)
    ax2.set_ylim(0, 35)

    plt.title("Elbow Method for Optimal K Selection (K-Means Clustering)", fontsize=13, fontweight="bold", pad=12)
    plt.tight_layout()
    out_path = os.path.join(PLOTS_DIR, "elbow_curve.png")
    plt.savefig(out_path, dpi=300)
    plt.close()
    logger.info("Saved Plot 1: %s", out_path)


def plot_silhouette_comparison(silhouette_df: pd.DataFrame, optimal_k: int):
    """Plot 2: Silhouette Score vs K with optimal K highlighted."""
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 5), dpi=300)

    ax.plot(
        silhouette_df["k"],
        silhouette_df["silhouette_score"],
        marker="s",
        linewidth=2.2,
        markersize=7,
        color="#7570b3",
        label="Silhouette Score",
    )
    ax.set_xlabel("Number of Clusters (K)", fontweight="bold")
    ax.set_ylabel("Mean Silhouette Coefficient", fontweight="bold")
    ax.set_xticks(silhouette_df["k"])
    ax.set_ylim(0.14, 0.26)
    ax.grid(True, linestyle="--", alpha=0.6)

    # Highlight peak/optimal K
    opt_row = silhouette_df[silhouette_df["k"] == optimal_k].iloc[0]
    ax.scatter([optimal_k], [opt_row["silhouette_score"]], color="#d62728", s=130, zorder=5, edgecolor="black", linewidth=1.5)
    ax.annotate(
        f"Peak Silhouette (K={optimal_k})\nScore = {opt_row['silhouette_score']:.4f}",
        xy=(optimal_k, opt_row["silhouette_score"]),
        xytext=(optimal_k + 0.6, opt_row["silhouette_score"] + 0.012),
        arrowprops=dict(facecolor="#d62728", shrink=0.08, width=1.5, headwidth=8),
        fontweight="bold",
        fontsize=10,
        bbox=dict(boxstyle="round,pad=0.4", facecolor="#ede7f6", edgecolor="#7570b3", alpha=0.9),
    )

    # Annotate weak-to-moderate boundary interpretation
    ax.axhline(0.25, color="gray", linestyle=":", alpha=0.7)
    ax.text(9.8, 0.245, "Weak-to-Moderate Threshold (0.25)", ha="right", fontsize=9, color="#555555", style="italic")

    plt.title("Silhouette Score Comparison Across Candidate K Values", fontsize=13, fontweight="bold", pad=12)
    plt.tight_layout()
    out_path = os.path.join(PLOTS_DIR, "silhouette_comparison.png")
    plt.savefig(out_path, dpi=300)
    plt.close()
    logger.info("Saved Plot 2: %s", out_path)


def plot_silhouette_analysis(X_train_scaled: np.ndarray, train_clusters: np.ndarray, optimal_k: int):
    """Plot 3: Silhouette plot showing silhouette coefficient for each sample in each cluster."""
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 6), dpi=300)

    sample_silhouette_values = silhouette_samples(X_train_scaled, train_clusters)
    avg_score = silhouette_score(X_train_scaled, train_clusters)

    y_lower = 10
    colors = ["#2b5c8f", "#d95f02", "#7570b3"]

    for i in range(optimal_k):
        ith_cluster_silhouette_values = sample_silhouette_values[train_clusters == i]
        ith_cluster_silhouette_values.sort()

        size_cluster_i = ith_cluster_silhouette_values.shape[0]
        y_upper = y_lower + size_cluster_i

        color = colors[i % len(colors)]
        ax.fill_betweenx(
            np.arange(y_lower, y_upper),
            0,
            ith_cluster_silhouette_values,
            facecolor=color,
            edgecolor=color,
            alpha=0.75,
            label=f"Cluster {i} (n={size_cluster_i})",
        )

        # Label cluster number in center of slice
        ax.text(-0.08, y_lower + 0.5 * size_cluster_i, f"Cluster {i}", color=color, fontweight="bold", fontsize=10)
        y_lower = y_upper + 15

    ax.set_title(f"Silhouette Analysis for K-Means Clustering (K={optimal_k})", fontsize=13, fontweight="bold", pad=12)
    ax.set_xlabel("Silhouette Coefficient Values", fontweight="bold")
    ax.set_ylabel("Cluster Slice (Sample Index)", fontweight="bold")

    # Average silhouette score vertical dashed line
    ax.axvline(x=avg_score, color="red", linestyle="--", linewidth=1.8, label=f"Mean Silhouette ({avg_score:.4f})")
    ax.set_yticks([])  # Clear y-axis tick labels
    ax.set_xlim([-0.2, 0.6])
    ax.legend(loc="upper right", frameon=True)
    ax.grid(True, linestyle="--", alpha=0.5)

    plt.tight_layout()
    out_path = os.path.join(PLOTS_DIR, "silhouette_analysis.png")
    plt.savefig(out_path, dpi=300)
    plt.close()
    logger.info("Saved Plot 3: %s", out_path)


def plot_pca_cluster_visualization(
    X_train_scaled: np.ndarray,
    train_clusters: np.ndarray,
    kmeans_model: KMeans,
    optimal_k: int,
):
    """Plot 4: 2D PCA projection of clusters with centroids marked."""
    pca = PCA(n_components=2, random_state=42)
    X_pca = pca.fit_transform(X_train_scaled)
    centroids_pca = pca.transform(kmeans_model.cluster_centers_)

    var_pc1 = pca.explained_variance_ratio_[0] * 100.0
    var_pc2 = pca.explained_variance_ratio_[1] * 100.0
    total_var = var_pc1 + var_pc2

    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 6), dpi=300)
    colors = ["#2b5c8f", "#d95f02", "#7570b3"]

    for i in range(optimal_k):
        mask = (train_clusters == i)
        ax.scatter(
            X_pca[mask, 0],
            X_pca[mask, 1],
            c=colors[i % len(colors)],
            label=f"Cluster {i} (n={np.sum(mask)})",
            alpha=0.60,
            s=28,
            edgecolors="none",
        )

    # Plot Centroids
    ax.scatter(
        centroids_pca[:, 0],
        centroids_pca[:, 1],
        marker="X",
        s=180,
        c="#ffffff",
        edgecolors="#000000",
        linewidths=2.2,
        zorder=10,
        label="Cluster Centroids (Projected)",
    )

    for i in range(optimal_k):
        ax.annotate(
            f"  C{i}",
            xy=(centroids_pca[i, 0], centroids_pca[i, 1]),
            fontweight="bold",
            fontsize=11,
            color="#000000",
            zorder=11,
        )

    ax.set_title("2D PCA Projection of K-Means Clusters (Standardized Feature Space)", fontsize=13, fontweight="bold", pad=12)
    ax.set_xlabel(f"Principal Component 1 ({var_pc1:.1f}% Variance)", fontweight="bold")
    ax.set_ylabel(f"Principal Component 2 ({var_pc2:.1f}% Variance)", fontweight="bold")
    ax.legend(loc="upper right", frameon=True, framealpha=0.9)
    ax.grid(True, linestyle="--", alpha=0.5)

    # Note at bottom explaining PCA is visualization-only
    ax.text(
        0.5, -0.13,
        f"Note: Clustering was performed strictly in 5D standardized feature space.\n"
        f"PCA captures {total_var:.1f}% of total variance and is used exclusively for 2D visual projection.",
        transform=ax.transAxes,
        ha="center",
        fontsize=8.5,
        color="#555555",
        style="italic",
        bbox=dict(boxstyle="square,pad=0.3", facecolor="#f8f9fa", edgecolor="#cccccc"),
    )

    plt.tight_layout()
    out_path = os.path.join(PLOTS_DIR, "pca_cluster_visualization.png")
    plt.savefig(out_path, dpi=300, bbox_inches="tight")
    plt.close()
    logger.info("Saved Plot 4: %s", out_path)


def plot_cluster_size_distribution(
    train_clusters: np.ndarray,
    val_clusters: np.ndarray,
    test_clusters: np.ndarray,
    optimal_k: int,
):
    """Plot 5: Grouped bar chart of cluster sizes across train, val, and test splits."""
    splits = ["Train", "Val", "Test"]
    cluster_labels = [f"Cluster {i}" for i in range(optimal_k)]

    data = {
        "Train": [np.sum(train_clusters == i) / len(train_clusters) * 100.0 for i in range(optimal_k)],
        "Val": [np.sum(val_clusters == i) / len(val_clusters) * 100.0 for i in range(optimal_k)],
        "Test": [np.sum(test_clusters == i) / len(test_clusters) * 100.0 for i in range(optimal_k)],
    }
    counts = {
        "Train": [np.sum(train_clusters == i) for i in range(optimal_k)],
        "Val": [np.sum(val_clusters == i) for i in range(optimal_k)],
        "Test": [np.sum(test_clusters == i) for i in range(optimal_k)],
    }

    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 5.5), dpi=300)
    x = np.arange(len(cluster_labels))
    width = 0.25

    colors = ["#2b5c8f", "#41b6c4", "#a1dab4"]

    for idx, split_name in enumerate(splits):
        bars = ax.bar(
            x + (idx - 1) * width,
            data[split_name],
            width,
            label=f"{split_name} (N={len(eval(split_name.lower() + '_clusters'))})",
            color=colors[idx],
            edgecolor="black",
            linewidth=0.8,
            alpha=0.85,
        )
        # Add labels on top of bars
        for b_idx, bar in enumerate(bars):
            cnt = counts[split_name][b_idx]
            pct = data[split_name][b_idx]
            ax.text(
                bar.get_x() + bar.get_width() / 2.0,
                bar.get_height() + 0.8,
                f"{cnt}\n({pct:.1f}%)",
                ha="center",
                va="bottom",
                fontsize=8,
                fontweight="bold",
            )

    ax.set_title("Cluster Proportion Consistency Across Partitions (Train / Val / Test)", fontsize=13, fontweight="bold", pad=12)
    ax.set_xlabel("Assigned Cluster", fontweight="bold")
    ax.set_ylabel("Proportion of Dataset (%)", fontweight="bold")
    ax.set_xticks(x)
    ax.set_xticklabels(cluster_labels, fontweight="bold")
    ax.set_ylim(0, max(max(v) for v in data.values()) + 12)
    ax.legend(loc="upper right", frameon=True)
    ax.grid(True, linestyle="--", alpha=0.5, axis="y")

    plt.tight_layout()
    out_path = os.path.join(PLOTS_DIR, "cluster_size_distribution.png")
    plt.savefig(out_path, dpi=300)
    plt.close()
    logger.info("Saved Plot 5: %s", out_path)

def plot_feature_distributions_by_cluster(train_df: pd.DataFrame, train_clusters: np.ndarray, optimal_k: int):
    """Plot 7: 5 subplots showing box plots of unscaled features across clusters."""
    df = train_df[FEATURE_COLS].copy()
    df["cluster"] = [f"Cluster {c}" for c in train_clusters]

    fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 3, figsize=(14, 9), dpi=300)
    axes = axes.flatten()

    colors = ["#2b5c8f", "#d95f02", "#7570b3"]

    for idx, feat in enumerate(FEATURE_COLS):

        sns.boxplot(
            data=df,
            x="cluster",
            y=feat,
            palette=colors,
            ax=ax,
            boxprops=dict(alpha=0.75, edgecolor="black"),
            medianprops=dict(color="yellow", linewidth=2.0),
            showmeans=True,
            meanprops=dict(marker="o", markeredgecolor="black", markerfacecolor="white", markersize=6),
        )
        ax.set_title(f"Distribution of {feat}", fontweight="bold", fontsize=11)
        ax.set_xlabel("")
        ax.set_ylabel("Original Feature Value", fontweight="bold", fontsize=10)
        ax.grid(True, linestyle="--", alpha=0.5, axis="y")

    # Hide unused 6th subplot
    axes[5].axis("off")

    # Add explanatory legend in 6th subplot area
    axes[5].text(
        0.1, 0.5,
        "Box Plot Interpretation:\n"
        "• Yellow line: Median\n"
        "• White circle: Mean\n"
        "• Shaded box: IQR (25th to 75th percentile)\n"
        "• Whiskers: 1.5 × IQR\n"
        "• Diamond points: Statistical outliers\n\n"
        "Clusters exhibit pronounced\n"
        "separation on semantic similarity\n"
        "and word count dimensions.",
        fontsize=10.5,
        bbox=dict(boxstyle="round,pad=0.6", facecolor="#f0f4f8", edgecolor="#b0bec5"),
        va="center",
    )

    plt.suptitle("Feature Distributions by Assigned K-Means Cluster (Training Set, N=1,264)", fontsize=14, fontweight="bold", y=0.98)
    plt.tight_layout()
    out_path = os.path.join(PLOTS_DIR, "feature_distribution_by_cluster.png")
    plt.savefig(out_path, dpi=300)
    plt.close()
    logger.info("Saved Plot 7: %s", out_path)


# ==============================================================================
# MAIN EXECUTION ROUTINE
# ==============================================================================

def run_kmeans_pipeline():
    """Execute complete Step 5 unsupervised learning workflow."""
    logger.info("=" * 80)
    logger.info("STARTING PART A - STEP 5: UNSUPERVISED LEARNING (K-MEANS CLUSTERING)")
    logger.info("=" * 80)

    ensure_directories()

    # 1. Load Data & Scaler
    train_df, val_df, test_df, scaler = load_data_and_scaler()

    # Extract strictly unscaled features
    X_train_raw = train_df[FEATURE_COLS].values
    X_val_raw = val_df[FEATURE_COLS].values
    X_test_raw = test_df[FEATURE_COLS].values

    # Transform using pre-fitted scaler (NO refitting)
    X_train_scaled = scaler.transform(X_train_raw)
    X_val_scaled = scaler.transform(X_val_raw)
    X_test_scaled = scaler.transform(X_test_raw)

    logger.info("Features scaled successfully using pre-fitted academic_scaler.pkl.")

    # 2. Evaluate K in [2..10]
    elbow_df, silhouette_df, models_dict = evaluate_k_range(
        X_train_scaled=X_train_scaled,
        k_min=2,
        k_max=10,
        random_state=42,
    )

    # 3. Select Optimal K
    # Peak silhouette is K=3 (0.2311) and elbow drop sharply flattens after K=3
    optimal_k = 3
    final_kmeans = models_dict[optimal_k]
    logger.info("Selected Optimal K=%d (Inertia: %.2f, Silhouette: %.4f)", optimal_k, final_kmeans.inertia_, silhouette_df.loc[silhouette_df['k'] == optimal_k, 'silhouette_score'].values[0])

    # 4. Predict Clusters for Train, Val, Test
    train_clusters = final_kmeans.labels_
    val_clusters = final_kmeans.predict(X_val_scaled)
    test_clusters = final_kmeans.predict(X_test_scaled)

    # 5. Save Model and Metadata
    model_save_path = os.path.join(CLUSTERING_DIR, "kmeans_model.pkl")
    joblib.dump(final_kmeans, model_save_path)
    logger.info("Serialized trained K-Means model to %s", model_save_path)

    # Invert cluster centers to original scale for interpretability
    centers_scaled = final_kmeans.cluster_centers_
    centers_unscaled = scaler.inverse_transform(centers_scaled)

    # 6. Cluster Profiling
    profile_df, summary_mean = compute_cluster_profiles(
        train_df=train_df,
        train_clusters=train_clusters,
        scaler=scaler,
        optimal_k=optimal_k,
    )

    # 7. Post-Hoc Target Label Comparison
    contingency_df, metrics_ari_nmi = compute_contingency_and_metrics(
        train_df=train_df,
        val_df=val_df,
        test_df=test_df,
        train_clusters=train_clusters,
        val_clusters=val_clusters,
        test_clusters=test_clusters,
    )

    # 8. Save Cluster Assignments
    for split_name, split_df, clusters in [
        ("train", train_df, train_clusters),
        ("val", val_df, val_clusters),
        ("test", test_df, test_clusters),
    ]:
        out_assign = split_df[["question", "answer", "target_label"] + FEATURE_COLS].copy()
        out_assign["cluster"] = clusters
        out_assign["cluster_name"] = [f"Cluster {c}" for c in clusters]
        csv_path = os.path.join(CLUSTERING_DIR, f"cluster_assignments_{split_name}.csv")
        out_assign.to_csv(csv_path, index=False)
        logger.info("Saved %s cluster assignments to %s", split_name, csv_path)

    # 9. Save Metadata JSON
    metadata = {
        "algorithm": "KMeans",
        "optimal_k": optimal_k,
        "random_state": 42,
        "n_init": 10,
        "max_iter": 300,
        "iterations_to_converge": int(final_kmeans.n_iter_),
        "inertia": round(float(final_kmeans.inertia_), 4),
        "silhouette_score": round(float(silhouette_df.loc[silhouette_df['k'] == optimal_k, 'silhouette_score'].values[0]), 4),
        "feature_names": FEATURE_COLS,
        "scaler_path": "ml/models/academic_scaler.pkl",
        "cluster_centers_scaled": centers_scaled.tolist(),
        "cluster_centers_unscaled": centers_unscaled.tolist(),
        "split_counts": {
            "train": {f"Cluster {c}": int(np.sum(train_clusters == c)) for c in range(optimal_k)},
            "val": {f"Cluster {c}": int(np.sum(val_clusters == c)) for c in range(optimal_k)},
            "test": {f"Cluster {c}": int(np.sum(test_clusters == c)) for c in range(optimal_k)},
        },
        "academic_contingency_metrics": metrics_ari_nmi,
        "neutral_cluster_descriptions": {
            "Cluster 0": "Cluster 0 - Extended / Substantive (Highest word count [20.0], highest lexical overlap [0.144], high semantic similarity [0.718], natural word repetition)",
            "Cluster 1": "Cluster 1 - Low Alignment / Divergent (Lowest semantic similarity [0.448], lowest lexical overlap [0.039], shortest word count [15.35], 0% Class 1)",
            "Cluster 2": "Cluster 2 - Concise Technical (High semantic similarity [0.717], highest average word length [6.83], highest unique word ratio [0.970], moderate length [17.2])",
        },
    }

    metadata_path = os.path.join(CLUSTERING_DIR, "cluster_metadata.json")
    with open(metadata_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        json.dump(metadata, f, indent=2)
    logger.info("Saved cluster metadata JSON to %s", metadata_path)

    # 10. Generate Visualizations (300 DPI)
    logger.info("Generating publication-quality visualizations (300 DPI)...")
    plot_elbow_curve(elbow_df, optimal_k)
    plot_silhouette_comparison(silhouette_df, optimal_k)
    plot_silhouette_analysis(X_train_scaled, train_clusters, optimal_k)
    plot_pca_cluster_visualization(X_train_scaled, train_clusters, final_kmeans, optimal_k)
    plot_cluster_size_distribution(train_clusters, val_clusters, test_clusters, optimal_k)
    plot_cluster_feature_heatmap(final_kmeans, optimal_k)
    plot_feature_distributions_by_cluster(train_df, train_clusters, optimal_k)

    logger.info("=" * 80)
    logger.info("PART A - STEP 5 K-MEANS PIPELINE COMPLETED SUCCESSFULLY!")
    logger.info("=" * 80)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    run_kmeans_pipeline()
```

### `ml/convert_hf_dataset.py`
```python
import json
from datasets import load_dataset


DATASET_NAME = "shimogerald/interview-coach-dataset"
OUTPUT_DIR = "ml/datasets/qa"


def convert_split(dataset, output_file):
    records = []

    for item in dataset:
        messages = item["messages"]

        question = None
        answer = None

        for message in messages:
            if message["role"] == "user":
                question = message["content"]

            elif message["role"] == "assistant":
                answer = message["content"]

        if question and answer:
            records.append({
                "question": question.strip(),
                "answer": answer.strip()
            })

    with open(output_file, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        for record in records:
            f.write(
                json.dumps(
                    record,
                    ensure_ascii=False
                ) + "\n"
            )

    print(f"{output_file}: {len(records)} records")


print("Loading Hugging Face dataset...")

dataset = load_dataset(DATASET_NAME)

convert_split(
    dataset["train"],
    f"{OUTPUT_DIR}/hf_train.jsonl"
)

convert_split(
    dataset["validation"],
    f"{OUTPUT_DIR}/hf_val.jsonl"
)

print("\nConversion completed.")
```

### `ml/create_target_scores.py`
```python
import os
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np


INPUT_FILE = "ml/datasets/features/train_features.csv"
OUTPUT_FILE = "ml/datasets/features/train_scored.csv"


print("========================================")
print("       CREATING TARGET SCORES")
print("========================================")


# Load feature dataset
df = pd.read_csv(INPUT_FILE)

print("Records:", len(df))


# -------------------------------------------------
# Semantic similarity score
# -------------------------------------------------

semantic_score = (
    df["semantic_similarity"]
    .clip(0, 1)
    * 100
)


# -------------------------------------------------
# Answer length score
# -------------------------------------------------
#
# Very short answers should receive less confidence.
# We use 80 characters as a reasonable minimum.
#

length_score = (
    df["answer_length"] / 80
).clip(0, 1) * 100


# -------------------------------------------------
# Final target score
# -------------------------------------------------
#
# Semantic quality is the main signal.
# Answer length provides a smaller contribution.
#

df["target_score"] = (
    semantic_score * 0.85
    + length_score * 0.15
)


# Keep score between 0 and 100

df["target_score"] = (
    df["target_score"]
    .clip(0, 100)
    .round(2)
)


# Save

os.makedirs(
    os.path.dirname(OUTPUT_FILE),
    exist_ok=True
)

df.to_csv(
    OUTPUT_FILE,
    index=False
)


print("\n========================================")
print("       TARGET SCORE CREATED")
print("========================================")

print("Records:", len(df))
print("Output:", OUTPUT_FILE)

print("\nTarget Score Statistics")
print("----------------------------------------")

print(
    df["target_score"].describe()
)

print("\nFirst 5 scores")
print("----------------------------------------")

print(
    df[
        [
            "question",
            "semantic_similarity",
            "answer_length",
            "target_score"
        ]
    ].head()
)

print("========================================")
```
